question.text: The position of an object travelling along the x-axis depends on time according to the equation X = 2t² + 4t − 6, where X is measured in metres and t in seconds. Determine the average velocity of the object from t = 0 to t = 2 s.
conditions: time interval from t = 0 to t = 2 s

solution.approach: Average velocity over an interval is the change in position divided by the change in time.

steps.text: Find the position at the two given times.
Divide the change in position by the change in time.

common_mistakes.text: Computing the instantaneous velocity dX/dt = 4t + 4 at t = 2 s and calling it the average velocity, giving 12 m/s.
Dividing X(2) alone by 2 as if the particle started from zero, giving 10/2 = 5 m/s.
